boot.//version: Fiction, like the maker and the group above it, and it is not maintained and must not be: it is the machine's firmware, not this repository's. A version in the UI that tracks the project rots by construction — a header here said M3 for six milestones. 3.07 is the one repo fact that is already frozen in the fiction's favour (the normative spec is HANDOFF-v3, its third revision) over a patch level that reads as a machine patched a few times and then left alone, which is the boot credit's joke: the bank and the manufacturer are the same group.

units.//: `~` and not `≈`, for the reason `Select.svelte` gives its caret: neither shipped font carries `≈`, and a tofu box in front of a number is worse than a rougher operator. It is also the more period one — a ROM character set of this vintage had no `≈` — and it pairs with the `<` that `walkingEta()` already prints below a minute.

qsa.//: What the meter's three levels mean, in a line each. QSA is a 1-to-5 signal report on a real set (R-29), and what this app puts on that scale is how much of the game a screen is being told — which is the same question, and the reason the gauge reads without a legend.
qsa.none: SIN ENLACE · no llega nada del servidor
qsa.4: ALCANCE 4 · tu equipo en tu sector
qsa.5: ALCANCE 5 · tu equipo en cualquier sitio

q.//: Q code, the signal abbreviations a radio operator already speaks. R-29 makes this game run on walkies, so it is the register the players are in — and a three-letter label reads at arm's length where a Spanish word does not.

select.//: The mark beside the chosen row of a dropdown. `>` and not `✓` because neither shipped font has `✓`, and a terminal menu’s own selector is what a missing tick should fall back to rather than a tofu box — the same call `Select.svelte` makes for its caret. Not `×`, which is the shape of §9.7’s ✕ and means a player is out.

sectors.title: SECTORES
sectors.hint: Pasa el ratón por una fila y se enciende en el mapa: los nombres no caben en el dibujo, así que esta lista es el índice. El ojo cierra terreno — en una zona la cierra a ella, en un sector cierra todas las suyas, y CERRAR DISTRITO cierra el pueblo entero. Cerrar quita sus zonas y sus puntos del mapa de todos los jugadores; tú sigues viendo el contorno apagado para poder reabrirlo. Se puede hacer EN CURSO — quien se quede dentro sigue emitiendo y tú lo sigues viendo, pero desaparece para los demás jugadores y deja de verlos. Queda en el registro.
